notes:
Summary: BrightForge is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace an expensive internal inference cluster and to get stronger SLAs for their customer-facing chat+search product. Primary driver is predictable latency for peak shopping hours (holiday spikes) and simpler ops. They want a POC that proves throughput guarantees at sustained load and proves p95/p99 SLOs under realistic traffic patterns. Key ask: a committed pool (reserved GPUs) sized so they can run a 3x redundancy plan and still hit peak TPS without cross-tenant interference.

Technical requirements (from SE workshop): p95 < 150ms for typical chat (avg prompt 120 tokens) at 200 concurrent users (approx 120 RPS sustained), p99 < 400ms under peak bursts, throughput headroom for 2x peak, support for sequence lengths up to 1024 tokens, KV cache warm-up within 30s for repeated sessions. Representative workload: mix = 60% chat small, 25% rerank/top-k, 15% embeddings for similarity lookup. They expect batching + dynamic routing to reduce unit cost but cannot accept >50ms added queuing latency.

Compliance: EU data residency for customer transcripts, SOC2 compliance required, SSO/SAML integration and KMS for key management. Legal flagged SLA termination/penalty language and want a performance credits clause. Procurement will need final quote and TCO comparison vs their on-prem cluster.

Quote from CTO on call: "We need a running cost model that beats our current spend by 25% after factoring in ops headcount. If Dedicated can't hit the SLOs consistently under soak, we won't move forward."
load_test_plan: Phase 0 - baseline: run single-model light load (10 GPU equiv) to validate kernel selection and batch size; capture p50/p95/p99; 6h run
Phase 1 - ramp: step concurrency 50 -> 200 -> 400 over 12h to measure linearity and autoscale behavior
Phase 2 - soak: 72h sustained at target peak (200 concurrent, 120 RPS) with periodic burst windows (400 RPS for 2 minutes every hour)
Phase 3 - failure modes: simulate node loss and fallback to variant models, measure cold-start impact and KV cache rebuild time
Phase 4 - quantization + batch tuning: test int8/4-bit quantized variants to compare cost/latency tradeoffs
representative_prompts: Chat small: 'Customer: I need to change my shipping address after placing order 8243. What steps do I follow?' (avg 90-150 tokens)
Rerank: 'Given 10 candidate FAQ paragraphs, score them for relevance to: refund after 45 days post-purchase'
Embedding: 'Encode product description for nearest-neighbor search: "Waterproof hiking jacket, men's, size L"'
Long-form: 'Summarize the following 800-token vendor policy into 3 bullet points'
poc_summary: Week 1 baseline: single-node perf matched expectations for small chat (p95 ~ 120ms), burst p99 spiked to ~420ms during warm cache
Week 2 ramp: linear throughput up to 180 RPS; at 240 RPS started seeing queue growth - resolved via larger batch window but added ~20ms median latency
Soak preparation: configuration locked for dedicated pool = 8 A100-equiv GPUs with reserved headroom of 2 nodes; planned soak start 2024-12-20
Risk items noted: legal SLA language, PCI scope around partial payment flows, and egress residency checks for EU customers
